_comment: ngsolve eigenvalue#3 (ArnoldiSolver needs both matrices; passing the same one twice forms the pencil, it does not fall back to an identity mass). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, unit_square maxh 0.2, H1 order 2, shift 1. Calling with a single matrix raises TypeError, so 'passing only A' is not reachable by accident. Passing a.mat twice raises NgException from the shift-and-invert factorisation with 'Numeric factorization failed', and the arithmetic reason is verified here rather than argued: A - shift*A assembled densely has max absolute entry exactly 0.0 at shift = 1, while A's own max entry is well above 1. An identity-mass fallback would have been visible -- the eigenvalues with a true identity mass differ from the generalised ones by 99.9% relative -- so the failure is not 'there was nothing to return'. Mutation: using shift 2.0 makes the pencil (1-shift)*A nonsingular and the fixture fails on pencil_is_exactly_zero_at_shift_one. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 moves SHIFT from 1.0 to 2.0, so the pencil A - shift*A = (1-shift)*A is -A rather than the zero matrix and the ArnoldiSolver(a.mat, a.mat, ...) call factorises without complaint. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 7 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'same_matrix_twice_raises=NgException', 'same_matrix_message_mentions_factorization=True', 'no_identity_fallback_happened=True' and 'pencil_is_exactly_zero_at_shift_one=True' (and prints the forbidden 'FAIL:') so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
